name: Food Prices and Affordability
definition: How expensive food and other household necessities are in the province, measured by changes in consumer, retail, wholesale and farmgate prices of staple and protein foods.
purpose: Price increases reduce what households can buy with the same income; this is the main short-term channel to food access in CALABARZON, a largely market-dependent region.
components: general food inflation (CPI food); cost of living (CPI headline); rice price (wholesale, retail); producer prices (farmgate palay, hog); protein prices (chicken, pork, tilapia); vegetable and root-crop prices
why_together: All measure the price a household or market pays for food. The 14 price series behave like about 4.6 independent signals: rice prices at wholesale, retail and farmgate move together (r 0.70-0.86, one rice component) and the bottom-30% CPI duplicates CPI food (r 0.94), while protein and vegetable prices move differently (|r| < 0.5 with CPI food).

name: Local Food Production and Supply
definition: Change in the quantity of food produced in the province: rice and corn, vegetables, root crops, fisheries and aquaculture, poultry and livestock.
purpose: A fall in local output tightens local supply and farm and fisher incomes; it is the availability side of food security.
components: cereals (palay, corn); vegetables; root crops; fisheries total (with aquaculture as a part); poultry; livestock
why_together: All are PSA quarterly production volumes for the same province. Commodity groups stay separate because their year-on-year changes are nearly unrelated (|r| <= 0.40; 6 series behave like 5.0 independent signals); aquaculture is not counted apart from the fisheries total it belongs to.

name: Climate and Weather Hazards
definition: Weather and climate conditions that can damage crops, fisheries, roads and livelihoods: rainfall and temperature departures, tropical cyclones near the province, and the ENSO state.
purpose: Hazards are the upstream cause of production losses and price spikes; separating them from production lets the model see both the hazard and its realized effect.
components: rainfall (total, anomaly); temperature anomaly; cyclones near the province (100 km, 300 km); cyclones in PAR (national); ENSO (ONI, PAGASA advisory)
why_together: All are physical hazard exposures, not food outcomes; production effects go to PS so a hazard and its consequence are not one indicator.

name: Household Income and Employment
definition: The ability of households to earn income: unemployment and underemployment, labour force participation, and OFW remittance inflows.
purpose: Income loss reduces food access even when prices are stable.
components: national unemployment (monthly LFS); provincial annual unemployment, underemployment and participation; national OFW remittances
why_together: Both employment and remittances are household income sources; national quarterly series and provincial annual series are kept at their own resolution.

name: Structural Poverty and Vulnerability
definition: Long-run conditions that make households in a province more likely to be food insecure when a shock arrives: poverty incidence, food poverty (subsistence incidence), the share of spending that goes to food, and population density.
purpose: Explains why the same shock hurts some provinces more; it changes slowly and is a profile, not a quarterly signal.
fao: Access (primary); Utilization (food poverty and diet budget, partial)
components: poverty incidence (SAE 2021); subsistence incidence (2021, 2023); FIES 2023 food share (all families and bottom 30%); population density (POPCEN 2024)
why_together: All are slow-moving household or population characteristics from PSA surveys or censuses; kept annual and never spread into quarters.
frequencies: static; static (2021); static (2024); triennial (2021, 2023); triennial (2023 only acquired)

name: Food Stress News Signals
definition: How much local and national news reports food shortage, price stress, job and income loss, or food assistance.
purpose: A possible early, near-real-time indication of stress that official statistics publish later.
components: provincial FSSI-v3 and article counts; national GDELT category shares
why_together: Both are media-derived signals with dated articles; they report perceptions, not measured conditions, so they are kept apart from the other indicators.

name: Experienced Hunger
definition: The share of families who report experiencing involuntary hunger (SWS Balance Luzon) and, for validation, survey-based food-insecurity experience (FIES) where it exists.
purpose: The outcome itself: the regional forecasting target and, lagged, its strongest predictor. It is the only directly measured food-insecurity condition available every quarter.
components: SWS Balance Luzon total hunger (target and lagged history); FNRI / CBMS FIES (validation)
why_together: Outcome measures are kept separate from the drivers so the framework never mixes cause and effect inside one indicator.
primary_use: regional forecasting target + its own history
